title: P0.27: Governed Local Fallback + External Failure Follow-up Continuity
description: After an external consultation (ChatGPT) was blocked by browser_security_verification, follow-up messages like 'pueddes solucionar eso' fell to Adaptive local orchestrator (~56s) instead of being recognized as deictic follow-ups of the external failure. The local fallback captured conversations that clearly belonged to the failed external consultation cycle.
reason: _EXTERNAL_FAILURE_FOLLOWUP_PATTERNS did not include deictic references ('eso', 'solucionar eso', 'arregla eso') or user-browser handoff patterns ('yo veo chatgpt', 'yo veo bien la ventana'). _try_handle_external_failure_followup matched only explicit retry/error keywords but missed pronoun-based follow-ups that refer to the recent failure context.
next_action: No further P0.27 action unless new runtime evidence shows deictic follow-ups after an external block entering local chat again. Separate unresolved capability remains: governed CDP/user-browser capture for using the user's existing Chrome session.
resume_hint: LIVE_VERIFIED on Windows runtime: 'has una consulta a chatgpt' blocked by ChatGPT security verification, then 'pueddes solucionar eso' was handled by external_failure_followup_deictic, emitted local_fallback_suppressed_for_external_failure, avoided Adaptive local orchestrator, resolved in 113.9ms, and left live_status idle.

metadata.root_cause: Bug: _EXTERNAL_FAILURE_FOLLOWUP_PATTERNS lacked deictic references ('eso', 'solucionar eso', 'arregla eso', 'pueddes solucionar eso'). When _last_external_failure_payload existed after a browser_security_verification block, the follow-up message 'pueddes solucionar eso' did not match any pattern and fell through to heavy local chat dispatch (~56s).
